title: What this means for energy traders — Monday, November 9, 2026

sections.overall: Geopolitics dominates the tape. Iran-related risk, an attack on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline and continued Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries all sit alongside a sharp weekly oil decline reported after the US midterms. Against that, the two confirmed trends, LNG deals with Asian buyers and corporate carbon removal purchases, are both STEADY: companies keep signing deals, but the pace has not changed this week.
sections.CRUDE_OIL: The digest pairs a sharp weekly fall in crude, tied to election results and Iran diplomacy hopes, with an attack on the Saudi East-West pipeline. Markets usually weigh outlet-capacity disruptions against demand and diplomacy signals, so the two stories pull in different directions. It is unclear how much export capacity the pipeline attack affects; the headline alone doesn't say. Strathcona's agreed merger with Greenfire and QatarEnergy's stake in a Chevron-operated Namibian licence show continued upstream deal-making.
sections.NATURAL_GAS: LNG remains the busiest theme. TotalEnergies' ADNOC supply and China offtake, Jera and Eneos Power's Sodegaura units, and an FT report on Qatar becoming the largest buyer of US LNG all point to long-dated contracting. Spot LNG shipping rates rose for a third week per Spark Commodities, which traders often read as tight vessel availability. EU coal burn rising year on year amid high gas prices is a reminder of fuel switching in Europe.
sections.REFINED_PRODUCTS: Supply-side stress is the story: Russia is rationing petrol after Ukrainian refinery strikes, and the FT reports US fuel supplies at a 20-year low as a diesel arrangement with Russia falters. EIA notes refiners have shifted yields toward middle distillates. These items are consistent with tight distillate balances, though the digest does not show current price levels.
sections.CARBON_CREDITS: EUAs rallied on Monday after two days of losses, helped by a strong auction. RGAs rose 11% week on week before dipping on Monday. Verra's first credits under its CCS methodology and the first ICVCM approval for coal-retirement transition credits point to new product categories maturing. In durable removal, a WBCSD and Climeworks Solutions report urges earlier buying, though it is advocacy rather than a purchase.
